proposals.sourceReason: 奢忌 means extravagance and jealousy or suspicion, not arrogance; 今則可一戰矣 is now then one can fight, so the EN must not substitute a different charge.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容皝
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容皝，字元真，廆第三子也。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang, whose courtesy name was Yuanzhen, was Murong Hui’s third son.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was the third son of Murong Hui.

sourceUnits.zh: 龍顏版齒，身長七尺八寸。
sourceUnits.en: He had an imperial bearing, unusually square teeth, and stood seven feet eight inches tall.
sourceUnits.literal: Dragon face and “plaque” teeth; body height seven chi eight cun.

sourceUnits.zh: 雄毅多權略，尚經學，善天文。
sourceUnits.en: He was bold, resourceful, devoted to the classics, and adept at reading the stars.
sourceUnits.literal: Heroic and resolute, abundant in stratagem; esteemed classical learning; skilled in astronomy.

sourceUnits.zh: 廆為遼東公，立為世子。
sourceUnits.en: When Murong Hui was named duke of Liaodong, Huang was made his heir.
sourceUnits.literal: When Hui became Duke of Liaodong, he was established as heir apparent.

sourceUnits.zh: 建武初，拜為冠軍將軍、左賢王，封望平侯，率眾征討，累有功。
sourceUnits.en: Early in the Jianwu era he was named general who champions the army and left worthy prince, created marquis of Wangping, and led troops on several successful expeditions.
sourceUnits.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, appointed General Who Champions the Army, Left Worthy Prince, enfeoffed Marquis of Wangping; led host in campaigns; repeatedly had merit.

sourceUnits.zh: 太甯末，拜平北將軍，進封朝鮮公。
sourceUnits.en: Late in the Taining era he became general who pacifies the north and was promoted to duke of Chaoxian.
sourceUnits.literal: At the end of Taining, appointed General Who Pacifies the North; advanced enfeoffment to Duke of Chaoxian.

sourceUnits.zh: 廆卒，嗣位，以平北將軍行平州刺史，督攝部內。
sourceUnits.en: When Hui died he succeeded him, serving as general who pacifies the north and acting governor of Pingzhou with authority over the whole command.
sourceUnits.literal: When Hui died, he succeeded the position; as general who pacifies the north acted as governor of Ping Province, supervising and holding the interior of the command.

sourceUnits.zh: 尋而宇文乞得龜為其別部逸豆歸所逐，奔死於外，皝率騎討之，逸豆歸懼而請和，遂築榆陰、安晉二城而還。
sourceUnits.en: Soon afterward Yuwen Qidegui was driven out by Yidougui of his separate division and died in exile; Huang led cavalry against Yidougui, who took fright and sued for peace; Huang then built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and withdrew.
sourceUnits.literal: Soon Yuwen Qidegui was by his separate division Yidougui expelled, fled and died outside; Huang led cavalry to campaign against him; Yidougui feared and requested peace; thereupon built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 咸康七年，皝遷都龍城。
sourceUnits.en: In the seventh year of Xiankang, he moved his capital to Longcheng.
sourceUnits.literal: In the seventh year of Xiankang, Huang moved the capital to Longcheng.

sourceUnits.zh: 率勁卒四萬，入自南陝，以伐宇文、高句麗，又使翰及子垂為前鋒，遣長史王寓等勒眾萬五千，從北置而進。
sourceUnits.en: He took forty thousand veterans through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and Murong Chui as van while Wang Yu led fifteen thousand from Beizhi.
sourceUnits.literal: Led picked soldiers forty thousand, entered from the southern defile to campaign against Yuwen and Goguryeo; again had Han and son Chui as vanguard, sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others leading host fifteen thousand to advance from Beizhi.

sourceUnits.zh: 高句麗王釗謂皝軍之從北路也，乃遣其弟武統精銳五萬距北置，躬率弱卒以防南陝。
sourceUnits.en: King Gao Zhao assumed the main thrust would come from the north, sent fifty thousand under his brother Wu to Beizhi, and held the southern defile with weaker troops.
sourceUnits.literal: Goguryeo King Zhao thought Huang’s army came by the northern route; thereupon sent his younger brother Wu leading picked fifty thousand to block Beizhi; personally led weak soldiers to guard the southern defile.

sourceUnits.zh: 翰與釗戰於木底，大敗之，乘勝遂入丸都，釗單馬而遁。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han routed him at Mudi, pressed into Wandu, and Zhao fled alone on horseback.
sourceUnits.literal: Han fought Zhao at Mudi, greatly defeated them, rode victory then entered Wandu; Zhao single horse fled.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝掘釗父利墓，載其屍並其母妻珍寶，掠男女五萬餘口，焚其宮室，毀丸都而歸。
sourceUnits.en: Huang opened Gao Zhao’s father Li’s tomb, carried off the corpse together with Zhao’s mother, wife, and treasures, plundered more than fifty thousand men and women, fired the palaces, razed Wandu, and returned.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang dug Zhao’s father Li’s tomb, loaded his corpse together with his mother, wife, and treasures, plundered over fifty thousand male and female, burned his palace chambers, destroyed Wandu and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 明年，釗遣使稱臣于皝，貢其方物，乃歸其父屍。
sourceUnits.en: The next year Gao Zhao sent envoys declaring himself a subject of Huang, offered local products, and Huang then returned his father’s corpse.
sourceUnits.literal: The next year, Zhao sent envoys declaring subject to Huang, offered their local products, then returned his father’s corpse.

sourceUnits.zh: 宇文歸遣其國相莫淺渾伐皝，諸將請戰，皝不許。
sourceUnits.en: Yuwen Gui sent Moqian Hun; Huang’s generals begged to fight but he refused.
sourceUnits.literal: Yuwen Gui sent his state chancellor Moqian Hun to campaign against Huang; the generals requested battle; Huang did not permit.

sourceUnits.zh: 渾以皝為憚之，荒酒縱獵，不復設備。
sourceUnits.en: Moqian Hun assumed Huang was afraid and gave himself to drink and hunting without precautions.
sourceUnits.literal: Hun because Huang feared them, indulged wine and wantonly hunted, again did not set defenses.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝曰：「渾奢忌已甚，今則可一戰矣。」
sourceUnits.en: Huang said, “Moqian Hun’s arrogance has peaked—now we can strike.”
sourceUnits.literal: Huang said: “Hun’s extravagance and jealousy are already extreme; now then can one battle.”

sourceUnits.zh: 遣翰率騎擊之，渾大敗，僅以身免，盡俘其眾。
sourceUnits.en: He sent Murong Han with cavalry to strike them; Moqian Hun was badly defeated and escaped alone, while his entire host was taken captive.
sourceUnits.literal: Sent Han leading cavalry to strike them; Hun was greatly defeated, barely himself escaped, wholly captured their host.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝躬巡郡縣，勸課農桑，起龍城宮闕。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang toured his domains, pushed farming and sericulture, and raised palaces at Longcheng.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang personally toured prefectures and counties, urged and supervised farming and sericulture, raised Longcheng palace and towers.

sourceUnits.zh: 尋又率騎二萬親伐宇文歸，以翰及垂為前鋒。
sourceUnits.en: He soon took twenty thousand horse against Yuwen Gui, with Murong Han and Murong Chui as van.
sourceUnits.literal: Soon again led cavalry twenty thousand personally to campaign against Yuwen Gui, with Han and Chui as vanguard.

sourceUnits.zh: 歸使其騎將涉奕於盡眾距翰，皝馳遣謂翰曰：「奕於雄悍，宜小避之，待虜勢驕，然後取也。」
sourceUnits.en: Yuwen Gui sent Sheyiyu to hold Murong Han; Huang sent word: “Sheyiyu is fierce—spar lightly until he grows reckless, then strike.”
sourceUnits.literal: Gui made his cavalry general Sheyiyu exhaust the host to resist Han; Huang gallop-sent word telling Han: “Sheyiyu is fierce and bold; ought slightly to avoid him, wait until the bandits’ situation grows arrogant, then take them.”

sourceUnits.zh: 翰曰：「歸之精銳，盡在於此，今若克之，則歸可不勞兵而滅。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han replied, “Yuwen Gui’s best troops are here; crush them and his realm falls without a long campaign.
sourceUnits.literal: Han said: “Gui’s picked troops are all here; now if we defeat them, then Gui can be destroyed without tiring the army.

sourceUnits.zh: 奕于徒有虛名，其實易與耳，不宜縱敵挫吾兵氣。」
sourceUnits.en: Sheyiyu is overrated and brittle—we must not let him sap our morale.”
sourceUnits.literal: Sheyiyu vainly has empty name; in truth he is easy to deal with; ought not to loose the enemy and blunt our army’s spirit.”

sourceUnits.zh: 於是前戰，斬奕於，盡俘其眾，歸遠遁漠北。
sourceUnits.en: He attacked, slew Sheyiyu, took his army, and drove Yuwen Gui deep into the steppe.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon advanced battle, beheaded Sheyiyu, wholly captured their host; Gui fled far to the northern desert.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝開地千餘里，徙其部人五萬餘落于昌黎，改涉奕於城為威德城。
sourceUnits.en: He annexed a thousand li of pasture, resettled fifty thousand Yuwen dependents at Changli, and renamed Sheyiyu’s fort Weide.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang opened territory over a thousand li, moved their division people over fifty thousand settlements to Changli, changed Sheyiyu city to Weide city.

sourceUnits.zh: 行飲至之禮，論功行賞各有差。
sourceUnits.en: He held a victory feast and handed out graded rewards.
sourceUnits.literal: Performed the “drink-on-arrival” rite, discussed merit and performed rewards each had gradations.

sourceUnits.zh: 以牧牛給貧家，田于苑中，公收其八，二分入私。
sourceUnits.en: Poor households received draft oxen to till the royal park on an eighty-twenty revenue split with the state.
sourceUnits.literal: Used herding oxen given to poor families, fields in the royal park, the public took eight-tenths, two-tenths went private.

sourceUnits.zh: 有牛而無地者，亦田苑中，公收其七，三分入私。
sourceUnits.en: Householders who owned cattle but no land tilled the park on a seventy-thirty split.
sourceUnits.literal: Those with oxen but without land, also fielded in the park, the public took seven-tenths, three-tenths went private.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝記室參軍封裕諫曰：臣聞聖王之宰國也，薄賦而藏于百姓，分之以三等之田，十一而稅之；
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang's secretary Feng Yu remonstrated: I have heard that a sage king keeps taxes light and stores wealth among the people, divides land into three grades, and levies one part in ten;
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang's secretary-advisor Feng Yu remonstrated, saying: Your servant has heard that when a sage king governs a state, he keeps taxes light and stores wealth among the people, divides land into three grades, and levies one part in ten;

approvedContextRepairs.after: He had a dragon countenance and plaque-like teeth, and stood seven chi eight cun tall.

He took forty thousand picked soldiers through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and his son Murong Chui as vanguard, and sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others leading fifteen thousand to advance from Beizhi.

King Gao Zhao assumed Huang’s army was coming by the northern route, so he sent his younger brother Wu leading fifty thousand picked troops to block Beizhi, and personally led weaker troops to guard the southern defile.
Yuwen Gui sent his state chancellor Moqian Hun against Huang; Huang’s generals begged to fight but he refused.
Murong Huang personally toured his prefectures and counties, urged farming and sericulture, and raised palaces at Longcheng.
He then advanced to battle, beheaded Sheyiyu, and wholly captured their host; Gui fled far to the northern desert.
